extracted.intended_audience: United Way national staff, local affiliate communications/design teams, vendors, and printers
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed brand identity guidelines for correct use, reproduction, localization, and file handling of the United Way brandmark across print, digital, merchandise and social media. Includes naming conventions for local affiliates and prohibited/acceptable treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brandmark components and meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The components of our brandmark – the rainbow of hope, the hand of support and the person as a symbol of humanity – communicate the important United Way brand characteristics — caring, inspiring, trustworthy and approachable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brandmark is joined with the United Way name in a permanent rectangular holding device. LIVE UNITED is no longer required as part of the United Way brandmark lockup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary full-color brandmark usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The full-color version of the United Way brandmark is the primary brandmark of the identity system and is required whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pantone spot color is preferred for corporate identity materials (business cards, letterhead, envelopes), office signage and merchandise. CMYK is for printed materials (brochures, reports) and RGB for on-screen, digital and video. All brandmark files are available on United Way Online. Never attempt to redraw or rescale the brandmark or add other graphic elements; do not extract graphic elements to use separately. Always display the registered trademark symbol (®) in the indicated position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control box use
rubrics_metrics.description: The control box is the white border that surrounds the logo and is used to create separation when the logo is placed on colored backgrounds without alternate logo color options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the control box to maintain consistent separation. Color variations between logos reflect optimization for each medium (spot/CMYK/RGB).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-color brandmark alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: When reproduction constraints prevent use of the primary full-color brandmark, use one of the alternative one-color versions. The white control box is still present in these solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-color blue brandmark is to be used when United Way Blue is the only available color. One-color black brandmark is to be used when black is the only available color. See United Way color palette for specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-use brandmark
rubrics_metrics.description: A special use brandmark has been developed for limited use; it may be reproduced in black, white or United Way Blue and does not require the white control box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for reproducing on fabric, plastic, glass or other materials used for merchandise or signage. Do not use special-use brandmarks on websites, four-color brochures or any application where full-color brandmark is usable. One-color brandmarks may not be reproduced in any color other than black, white or United Way Blue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear space requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear space frames the logo and separates it from other elements including text and the edge of printed materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The logo must be surrounded with at least the required minimum clear space which is determined by 1/2 the height of the symbol square.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum size requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum reproduction sizes are specified to ensure legibility and brand recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen (RGB) minimum size: 90 pixels or 1.25” wide. Print (CMYK) and One Color minimum size: 0.75” wide. Special Usage minimum size: 0.75” wide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable uses (prohibitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific alterations and misuses of the brandmark that are prohibited to maintain consistent and correct application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never alter the colors in the brandmark; never tilt the brandmark; never distort its shape; never add elements inside the brandmark; never rearrange the elements of the brandmark; never alter the shape of the brandmark; never change the font or color of the local identifier; never substitute type in the brandmark; never put other words or phrases inside the brandmark; never extract any of the graphic elements or words 'United Way' contained in the brandmark to use separately. The circle and square mark may be extracted only for social media profiles and must not be used otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered trademark display
rubrics_metrics.description: The brandmark must include the registered trademark symbol to ensure legal rights are protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always display the registered trademark symbol (®) in the position indicated on the brandmark artwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Artwork files follow a specific naming convention containing abbreviated information about the file; file names are lowercase and use dashes to separate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: united-way-lockup-cmyk.eps, united-way-lockup-spot.eps, united-way-lockup-spot-black.eps, united-way-lockup-black-special.eps. Parts of the file name indicate company, color (CMYK/Spot/RGB/blue/black/white), version (special) and format suffix (.eps). Use .eps vector artwork to create other formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artwork file selection guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on which brandmark file variation to use depending on reproduction method and medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use four-color process file when documents contain full-color photographs. Use spot-color file when four spot colors will be printed (e.g., silk-screened items). Use three-color spot file to provide full color while printing in three inks. Use RGB file for on-screen, digital, web and video. Use one-color file when United Way Blue (Pantone 287) is the only available color. Use special-use blue/black/white for reproductions where screening of inks isn't possible or on non-paper surfaces, faxes/photocopies, or dark backgrounds as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldwide naming convention (tiers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardized naming arrangements for countries, regions and cities to clarify local organization names within the larger brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 1 (Worldwide Brands and Countries): preferred arrangement 'United Way' first, 'Country Name' second (e.g., United Way Australia). Second preferred: 'United Way of Country' (e.g., United Way of India). Tier 2 (International countries with city-based offices): preferred 'United Way of City' (e.g., United Way of Delhi). Second preferred: 'United Way' first, then 'City Name' (e.g., Mile High United Way).

rubrics_metrics.name: United States naming convention (tiers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardized naming arrangements for U.S. local entities with guidance for city, region, and regional/city-based offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred arrangement for city names is 'United Way of' + 'City Name' (e.g., United Way of New York City). Second preferred is 'City Name' + 'United Way' (e.g., Mile High United Way). For regions, 'Region' + 'United Way' is preferred; second option is 'United Way of Region.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Brandmark localization constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: Three available constructs for logo localizations across local communications: Vertical (recommended), Horizontal Left, Horizontal Right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These localizations use precise proportional relationships that should not be altered. The brandmark with local identifier must always appear as shown in one of the illustrated variations; never redraw or rescale the local identifier or add graphic elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical localization specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Precise localization option for vertical lockups with placement and sizing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best for brochures, flyers, posters. Local identifier can extend to a maximum of three lines. Line character guidance: LINE 1 and LINE 3 options (20–23 characters per line). Local identifier is placed in a fixed position relative to the brandmark holding shape. When on a colored background, the white control box expands to hold the local identifier. The local identifier may be decreased slightly in size to fit when it extends beyond the width by only two or three letters. Proportional units (e.g., 1U, 1/2U, 1/4U) define spatial relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontal left localization specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Localization option for left-aligned horizontal lockups with multiple width options and spacing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best for signage/banners and horizontal merchandise (pens, pencils). Five width localization options were created with specific character counts per line: WIDTH 1 (up to 10 chars), WIDTH 2 (11–15), WIDTH 3 (16–21), WIDTH 4 (22–27), WIDTH 5 (28–32). After sizing and alignment, there must be equal spacing above, below and to the left side of localization text within the white control box (Let X = X = X). Minimum clearances measured in 1/2 square units apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontal right localization specifications (digital only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Localization option for right-aligned horizontal lockups intended for digital applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This option is for digital use only (RGB). Best for websites, email, desktop and mobile. Uses the same five width localization options (WIDTH 1–5) with minimum clearances and equal spacing (Let X = X = X). Minimum clearance measured as 1/2 square applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media brandmarks and permitted extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the United Way symbol mark for small-screen social engagement and rules for square/circle marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social media brandmarks are to be used for social media applications only; use elsewhere is not permitted. The square mark should only be used for profiles that display pictures as squares (Facebook). The circle mark should only be used for profiles that display pictures as circles (Pinterest, Instagram, Twitter). Examples of correct and incorrect usages are provided.
